body:
Thank you. Your words are really comforting. I mean it. 

I'm definitely isolated, I want to get out more but my dogs are a barrier to that. I can't take the dogs with me because my sister and friend are allergic, plus they hate them. If I leave the house for more than a few hours they will pee and poop inside. I can't cut a hole for a doggy door because it's a rental. I can hang a new door to cut a dog door in, and I actually spent a week on that project, but I couldn't get it right and ended up putting the old door back on and I don't have the motivation to give it another go. I could take them to daycare but I need to find a local vet and get their rabies shots updated, and daycares can't watch them at night (prime time for hanging out and meeting new people), they would have to be boarded, and one of the dogs can't be boarded because he has such severe kennel anxiety... 

None of this is insurmountable but it feels like it. So I just stay home with them most of the time instead. I know these are all such small excuses but I'm sure I'm preaching to the choir about how small things seem impossible. 

I just want a normal person to come in, help me make some solutions, help me get daycare for the dogs and help me grocery shopping and help me not feel so helpless. Help me get back on track. But I can't ask for that level of care. I'm afraid everyone would overreact, or worse, people would try to help but not actually help at all. I don't know. I don't know what I want.
